```{r}
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(tidyverse)
library(cluster)
```


```{r}
df<- read.csv("genz_digital_lifestyle_tech_habits.csv")
str(df)
summary(df)
```
```{r}
#Move UserID to row names (it will no longer be a column)
df<- df %>% column_to_rownames(var="User_ID")
```


```{r}
#for memory of R behind the scene 'order' or 'factor'
df$Tech_Savviness <- ordered(df$Tech_Savviness, levels=c("Beginner", "Intermediate", "Advanced", "Expert"))
df$Privacy_Awareness_Level <- ordered(df$Privacy_Awareness_Level, levels=c("Low", "Medium", "High"))
df$Gaming_Activity <- ordered(df$Gaming_Activity, levels=c("Never", "Occasional", "Frequent"))

df$Preferred_Device <- factor(df$Preferred_Device)
df$Gender <- factor(df$Gender)
```


```{r}
#need to treat the two groups differently - standardization or one-hot encoding
num_cols <- c("Age", "Daily_Screen_Time_hrs", "Social_Media_Usage_hrs", "Streaming_Subscriptions")
cat_cols <- c("Gender", "Preferred_Device", "Gaming_Activity", "Tech_Savviness", "Privacy_Awareness_Level")

#splitting the original df into two
df_num <- df[ , num_cols] #the blank space >> keep all rows, but only num_cols
df_cat <- df[ , cat_cols]

```


```{r}
res_pca <- PCA(
  df_num,
  scale.unit = TRUE, # standardize variables
  ncp = ncol(df_num),  # max number of PCs
  graph = FALSE
)
#Kaiser Criterion (Eigenvalue>1)
```


```{r}
res_pca$eig  #eigenvalue table
fviz_eig(res_pca, addlabels = TRUE)   #scree plot
```


```{r}
n_pc <- 2  #choose based on eig / scree
pca_coords <- res_pca$ind$coord[ , 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE]  #res_pca may include eigenvalues, variable information, individual information, etc..(pca treats rows as individuals) So, extract ind, take all rows and the columns/components up to n_pc; drop=FALSE >> not to turn it into a vector/ a simple list of numbers
```


```{r}
res_mca <- MCA(
  df_cat,
  ncp = ncol(df_cat)*2,  #just increased the total components. but lower than the result (no of total category levels - no of total variables)
  graph = FALSE
)
```


```{r}
res_mca$eig
fviz_eig(res_mca, addlabels = TRUE)
```


```{r}
nrow(res_mca$eig)      # should be 13  (MCA always computes the full spectrum)
ncol(res_mca$ind$coord)    # should be 10 (no of dimensions kept in the coordinate matrices) the first 10
```
```{r}
n_mc <- 2
mca_coords <- res_mca$ind$coord[ ,1:n_mc, drop=FALSE]
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```


```{r}
#combine num & cat factor scores into a single matrix
cluster_data <- cbind(pca_coords, mca_coords) # just joining the df, not naming
colnames(cluster_data) <- c(
  paste0("PC", 1:n_pc), #PC prefix is f/b 1,2,3 from 1:n_pc
  paste0("MC", 1:n_mc)
)
```


```{r}
cluster_data_scaled <- scale(cluster_data)
#although input as df, R returns a matrix; stores original means and SDs as hidden attributes (scaled: center & scaled: scale)
```


```{r}
#compute distance matrix & run Ward's hierarchical clustering
dist_mat <- dist(cluster_data_scaled, method = "euclidean")
hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "ward.D2")
```


```{r}
k_range <- 2:7 #whatever range
sil_results <- data.frame(k=integer(), sil = numeric()) #creates an empty dataframe
for (k in k_range) {
  #cut the tree into k clusters
  c1 <- cutree(hc, k = k) #c1 will be a list of cluster assignments
  
  #Compute silhouette
  sil <- silhouette(c1, dist_mat)
  sil_mean <- mean(sil[, "sil_width"]) #sil object contains a 'width' for every single row
  
  sil_results <- rbind(
    sil_results,
    data.frame(k=k, sil = sil_mean)
  )
}                          
sil_results
```


```{r}
plot(sil_results$k, sil_results$sil, type = "b",
     xlab = "Number of clusters k",
     ylab = "Mean silhouette width",
     main = "Silhouette vs k (Hierarchical Clustering on PCA+MCA)")
```

```{r}
fviz_dend(
  hc,
  k = k_chosen,
  type = "circular",
  show_labels = FALSE, 
  lwd = 0.1,             # Use 0.1 for maximum definition
  k_colors = "npg",
  main = "Hierarchical clustering on PCA+MCA scores"
) +
theme_void()             # This removes the background grid/axis for a cleaner look

```

```{r}
#scree plot for PCA
fviz_eig(res_pca, addlabels = TRUE, ylim = c(0,100)) + ggtitle("PCA - variable explained")
```


```{r}
#individuals in PCA space, colored by cluster
fviz_pca_ind(
  res_pca,
  axes = c(1,2), #PC1 on x and PC2 on y
  habillage = df$cluster, #colors the points based on the clusters & maps the groups back onto the pca coordinates
  addEllipses = TRUE,
  ellipse.type = "norm",
  palette = "jco",
  geom = "point", #this line hides the crowded label
  repel = TRUE #for safety for geom
) +
  ggtitle("Individuals on PCA (numeric) axes, colored by cluster")
```


```{r}
#pca variables
fviz_pca_var(
  res_pca,
  axes = c(1,2),
  col.var = "contrib",
  gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"),
  repel = TRUE,
  labelsize = 4.5,
  arrowsize = 1
) +
  ggtitle ("PCA variable factor map (numeric variables)")
```


```{r}
fviz_eig(res_mca, addlabels = TRUE) + ggtitle("MCA - inertia explained")
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

var <- get_mca_var(res_mca) #it returns a list containing $coord, $cos2, $contrib, $inertia
var_df <- as.data.frame(var$coord) #choose $coord

#Rename first 2 dimensions for convenience
colnames(var_df)[1:2] <- c("Dim1", "Dim2")

#Sanity check
nrow(var_df)
head(rownames(var_df))
```


```{r}
#cat variables in the same order used in MCA
cat_cols <- colnames(df_cat)

#Number of levels per variable
lev_counts <-sapply(df_cat, nlevels)
lev_counts
sum(lev_counts) #should equal nrow(var_df)

#Build 'variable' as: var1 repeated nlevels(var1) times, then var2, etc. (get_mca_var gives the coordinates for the levels, but it isn't clean)
var_df$variable <- rep(cat_cols, times = lev_counts)

#The level label is just the row name (e.g. "Female", "Own")
var_df$level <- rownames(var_df)

#Nice label: "Variable:Level"
var_df$label <- paste(var_df$variable, var_df$level, sep = ":")

#Check
unique(var_df$variable)
length(unique(var_df$variable))
```

```{r}
ggplot(var_df, aes(x = Dim1, y = Dim2, colour = variable, shape = variable)) + 
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "MCA category map (coloured by variables)",
    x = "Dim 1",
    y = "Dim 2",
    colour = "Variable",
    shape = "Variable"
  )
```

```{r}
head(num_cols)
```

```{r}
num_cols <- colnames(df_num) #to create the whitelist of the column names automatically (excluding unnecessary columns) for summarise func

cluster_means <- df %>% #receives df as input and produce df or (tibble) as output.
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(num_cols), mean, na.rm = TRUE)) #na.rm > ignore the missing piece

cluster_means
```


```{r}
library(reshape2)

cm_scaled <- cluster_means
cm_scaled[ , num_cols] <- scale(cm_scaled[ , num_cols]) #scale() turns the columns into a matrix; then cm_scaled > back to df

cm_long <- melt(cm_scaled, id.vars = "cluster", variable.name = "variable", value.name = "z") #melt() changes the table from 'Wide' to 'Long' as ggplot requires 'tidy' data where every row is a single observation (X= variable, Y=cluster, z=fill color)

ggplot(cm_long, aes(x = variable, y = as.factor (cluster), fill = z)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#4575b4", mid = "white", high = "#d73027") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Cluster profiles for numeric variables (z-scores)",
    x = "",
    y = "Cluster"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


```


```{r}
cat_cols <- colnames(df_cat)  # or c("ord1","ord2","ord3","nom1","nom2")

for (v in cat_cols) {
  p <- ggplot(df, aes_string(x = "cluster", fill = v)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Distribution of", v, "by cluster"),
      y = "Proportion",
      x = "cluster"
    )
  print(p)
}
```
